tap-2012.notes: Source 1 copy is the 2015 front page of the TAP site (belongs to tap-2015). Source 2 is the association's general home page.

sources.evidence: The front page as it stood in September 2015 announces the 5th Torneo Argentino de Programación on 26 September 2015 and reports the 2014 edition; nothing in it concerns the 2012 edition.
The page is the home page of the Asociación Argentina de Programación Competitiva with a calendar for 2026, not a page of the 2012 edition.

tap-2013.notes: Source 3 is an announcement before the contest; no results. Sources 1 and 2 copies are other pages (2015 TAP front page, association home page).

sources.evidence: The front page as it stood in September 2015 announces the 5th Torneo Argentino de Programación on 26 September 2015 and reports the 2014 edition; nothing in it concerns the 2013 edition.
The page is the home page of the Asociación Argentina de Programación Competitiva with a calendar for 2026, not a page of the 2013 edition.
Blog post dated 28 July 2013 titled 3er Torneo Argentino de Programación announcing the tournament of 5 October 2013.

tap-2014.notes: Source 3 file is a GitHub HTML viewer page saved with a .pdf name; its raw PDF link is on the page but was not fetched.

sources.evidence: Table of 66 team rows with columns Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time, Medal, Citation and Site citation.
The held file is the GitHub web page for docs/tap2014-problems.pdf in a repository (HTML with GitHub navigation and a sign-in link), not the PDF itself.

tap-2015.notes: Page says 75 teams; catalogue note says 87. The rankings role is partial (champion, runner-up, 5th, 6th and site winners only). The problemset role rests on a link to a PDF that is not in this page.

sources.evidence: News item titled Resultados del Torneo Argentino de Programación TAP 2015 giving the champion, runner-up, 5th, 6th and each site's winner, with a link to the problems PDF.

tap-2020.notes: s1 is a combined BOCA board of several countries (1178 teams); the AR rows number 54 against 53 in s2, one extra Argentine row not checked. The BOCA title is only 'Score Page'; s1 is catalogued as subbr-2020 on the host.

sources.evidence: The BOCA Final Scoreboard lists teams of Argentina (54 user names ending /AR, with TAP universities such as FAMAF - UNC) among 1178 teams of a shared Latin American subregional board.
The page is titled 'Torneo Argentino de Programación 2020 — standings' and has a table of 53 ranked teams with Argentine institutions.
